facts: Campbell County is selling Spaeth Ranch, 5,000 county-owned acres southeast of Cam-plex, Gillette, Wyoming
All three bidders for Spaeth Ranch want a data center on the site
Peabody offered $13 million for a 300-megawatt energy and tech park
Peabody offered $13 million for the 5,289-acre Spaeth Ranch near Gillette, where it would build a power plant and two data centers
Three proposals for the ranch were submitted: Peabody $13 million, Central Southwest Texas Development $15 million, Range Sustain Grange $10.5 million; the county paid $10 million

facts: Platte County Planning & Zoning board held a public hearing the week before 2026-09-01 on rezoning over 5,000 acres of private land
Planning & Zoning approved the rezoning for Site Layer 4, with a commissioner hearing to follow
Platte County Planning & Zoning board held a public hearing last week on rezoning over 5,000 acres of private land
Planning & Zoning approved the rezoning for Site Layer 4 ahead of a county commissioner hearing
Site Layer 4, LLC is seeking a rezone of 5,344 acres of ranchland northeast of Wheatland, WY.
Platte County Planning and Zoning Commission unanimously recommended approval on August 26, 2026.
Platte County commissioners are scheduled to vote on the rezone on September 2, 2026.
No megawatt figures, construction timelines or construction application have been filed; project is in Phase 1 site evaluation.
Platte County Planning and Zoning Commission voted unanimously on Aug 26, 2026 to recommend rezoning 5,344 acres to industrial.
Platte County commissioners are set to decide on the rezoning on Sept 2, 2026 at 1 p.m.
The project is in Phase 1 (site evaluation and feasibility); no megawatt figures or square footage have been made public.
A special-use permit with separate public review is required after rezoning.
Platte County P&Z unanimously recommended rezoning 5,344 acres northeast of Wheatland from RAM to industrial.
Rezone request goes before county commissioners at 1 p.m. Sept. 2, 2026.
Conditions: revert to RAM if construction hasn't begun within five years, subdivision goes to commissioners, special-use permit required.
Land is owned by Gregor and Cindy Goertz.
Public comment lasted about two hours with a roughly even split of support and opposition.
Platte County planning staff proposed adding a definition of "data center" to county rules.
Data centers would require conditional special-use permits under the proposed edits.
Proposed edits would place data centers in existing industrial and commercial chapters rather than a separate chapter.
A public hearing is scheduled for Sept. 16 at the Agriplex.
Commissioners supported using the conditional permit tool.
